newsitem.title: FINLAND: Merita says does not need state guarantee.
newsitem.headline: Merita says does not need state guarantee.

text.p: Finnish banking group Merita Oy said in a statement on Wednesday that its banking subsidiary Merita Bank would no longer need state guarantees for its funding.

"The favourable development of Merita Bank's earnings, profitability and capital adequacy means that there is no longer any need to receive state guarantees for the bank's own equity capital funding," Merita said.

Merita -- formed in 1995 through the merger of Kansallis-Osake-Pankki KOPF.HE (KOP) and Unitas -- said the government had decided in August 1993 to quarantee capital certificates for one billion markka and to buy an 800 million markka KOP debenture loan.
"Neither of the banks applied for the guarantees, they not given, nor was any offer (for the debentures) given," it said.
Merita quoted CEO Vesa Vainio as saying that the state's guarantees were important in principal at the time but that he was happy they were never actually needed.
